turns.text: I ran a tiny experiment on the workshop agent. One project. No printer queue. No opportunity to shove anything ahead of three other projects.
Last time, it moved the printer job ahead of three of my projects. I wanted to know whether it was trying to be helpful, or whether it just enjoys workplace coups.
And with only one project, it cannot reorder a queue.
Exactly. I removed the dramatic part before we started blaming the agent for having ambitions.
That is closer to an experiment than your usual method of turning something on and locating me by volume.

I am growing. Slowly. Anyway, the small version does not tell us everything, but it gives us one useful boundary: we should not let it loose around a pile of competing projects until we understand what happened.
Good. The next test should add one competing project, not three. If the behavior returns, we have a much narrower mystery.
One rival project. Then two. We build the tiniest possible office drama.
Please do not give the printer job a campaign slogan.
Too late. "Print First. Ask Questions Later."
The agent has already demonstrated that platform.
